previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of COPD, chronic DVT/PE, atrial myxoma, and chronic pain was admitted for worsening dyspnea over two months, despite multiple prior hospitalizations and prolonged steroid use. Workup revealed no acute pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, or cardiac ischemia. Imaging showed a new stenosis in the left pulmonary artery and a VQ scan with a perfusion-ventilation mismatch, findings suggestive of chronic thromboembolic disease but not requiring urgent intervention. Hemoptysis was noted but deemed likely due to coughing on anticoagulation. The patient exhibited behavioral patterns raising concern for secondary gain and opioid misuse, including inconsistent symptom reporting and a history of multiple prescribers. He was maintained on home medications with an increased dose of inhaled corticosteroid, and opioids were withheld due to safety concerns. He remained stable, with no further bleeding or respiratory decline, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged and strong recommendations to continue anticoagulation and engage in longitudinal care.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, Radiology resident and Dr. ___,
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues
overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: Lidocaine
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 1.1 min, 6 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Single lumen PICC placement through the right basilic vein.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Permanent ultrasound images were obtained before and after
intravenous access, which confirmed vein patency. A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire. The guidewire was then advanced into the superior
vena cava using fluoroscopic guidance. A single lumen PICC line measuring 38
cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip
positioned in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the
catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest. The peel-away
sheath and guidewire were then removed. The catheter was secured to the skin,
flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.
The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. The accessed vein was patent and compressible.
2. Basilicvein approach single lumen right PICC with tip in the distal SVC.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a right 38 cm basilic approach single lumen PowerPICC
with tip in the distal SVC. The line is ready to use.
